variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
(define x 10)
(define y 20)

;; Local variables
(let ((a 1)
      (b 2))
  (+ a b))

;; Sequential binding (let*)
(let* ((a 1)
       (b (+ a 1)))
  b)
variables.notes: define creates top-level bindings. let creates parallel local bindings, while let* allows bindings to refer to previous ones.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
42                   ; integer
3.14                 ; inexact real (float)
3/4                  ; exact rational
3+4i                 ; complex number
"Hello"              ; string
#\A                  ; character
'symbol              ; symbol
'(1 2 3)             ; list
#(1 2 3)             ; vector
#t                   ; boolean true
#f                   ; boolean false
data_types.notes: Scheme implements a full numeric tower. Boolean values are #t and #f. Lists are built from cons cells.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
(+ 1 2 3)    ; => 6
(- 10 4)     ; => 6
(* 2 3)      ; => 6
(/ 10 2)     ; => 5

(= 1 1)      ; Numeric equality
(equal? "a" "a") ; Deep structural equality
(eqv? 'a 'a) ; Value equality
(eq? 'a 'a)  ; Pointer equality

(and #t #f)  ; => #f
(or #f #t)   ; => #t
(not #t)     ; => #f
operators.notes: Operators are prefix functions. Scheme uses standard predicate names ending in ? for type and equality checks.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: if is used for simple branching. cond is used for multi-way if-else chains. case matches against discrete values.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
;; Traditional looping construct using `do`
(do ((i 0 (+ i 1)))
    ((= i 10))
  (display i)
  (newline))

;; Iterating over a list
(for-each (lambda (x) (display x))
          '(1 2 3))
for_loop.notes: Scheme favors recursion over imperative loops, but do provides standard iteration. for-each and map are used for list iteration.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
;; Named let for looping
(let loop ((x 0))
  (when (< x 10)
    (display x)
    (newline)
    (loop (+ x 1))))

;; Using mutation
(let ((x 0))
  (let loop ()
    (when (< x 10)
      (display x)
      (set! x (+ x 1))
      (loop))))
while_loop.notes: Named let is the idiomatic way to express loops in Scheme through tail recursion. The compiler optimizes this into a standard loop.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
;; Standard definition
(define (add a b)
  (+ a b))

;; Equivalent lambda binding
(define add (lambda (a b) (+ a b)))

;; Variadic function
(define (sum . numbers)
  (apply + numbers))
functions.notes: Functions are first-class citizens created with lambda. define provides shorthand syntax for defining named functions.

arrays.title: Arrays (Vectors)
arrays.code:
;; Creating a vector
(make-vector 5 0)
#(1 2 3 4 5) ; Literal syntax

;; Accessing and modifying
(define v (vector 10 20 30))
(vector-ref v 0)       ; => 10
(vector-set! v 0 42)   ; Mutates vector
arrays.notes: Vectors provide O(1) access. Scheme uses -ref for accessing and -set! for mutating. The ! suffix indicates a mutating operation.

maps.title: Maps (Hash Tables)
maps.code:
;; SRFI 69 Hash Tables
(define ht (make-hash-table equal?))

;; Setting values
(hash-table-set! ht "key" "value")

;; Getting values
(hash-table-ref ht "key")
(hash-table-ref/default ht "missing" "default")

;; Checking existence
(hash-table-exists? ht "key")
maps.notes: Hash tables are typically provided via SRFI 69 or R6RS/R7RS standard libraries, supporting custom equivalence predicates.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
(guard (e ((error-object? e) (display "Error occurred") 0)
          (else (raise e)))
  (/ 1 0))

;; Signaling an error
(error "Something went wrong")
error_handling.notes: R7RS uses guard for exception handling, which acts like a try-catch block with cond-style clauses for matching exceptions.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
;; Single-line comment in Lisp
#|
 Multi-line block comment
|#
(defun add (a b)
  "Documentation string for function"
  (+ a b))
comments.notes: Scheme uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.code:
(def x 42)          ; Integer
(def pi 3.14159)    ; Float
(def ratio 1/3)     ; Exact rational ratio
(def hex #xFF)      ; Hexadecimal
numbers.notes: Scheme supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.notes: Scheme treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Scheme performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.code:
(def s "Hello, World!")
(def char-val (char s 0))
(def multi "Line 1
Line 2")
strings.notes: Scheme represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Scheme formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Scheme, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Scheme constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.notes: Scheme achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.notes: Scheme emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Scheme are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Scheme uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Scheme provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.notes: Scheme isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
